The part of a tree that grows underground is the **roots**.

Regarding the time period, the text provides several strong contextual clues pointing to the **Victorian Era** (specifically the mid-to-late 19th century, roughly 1837–1901).

1.  **Gas Lighting and Horse-Drawn Carriages:** These were the dominant modes of urban infrastructure and transportation in major cities during the 19th century before the widespread adoption of electricity and automobiles.
2.  **Architecture (Georgian and Victorian):** The mention of Victorian architecture explicitly places the setting in the 19th century. Georgian architecture (1714–1830) often preceded or coexisted with early Victorian styles in established cities.
3.  **Charles Dickens:** Charles Dickens was a prolific author whose most famous works were published between the 1830s and 1870s. The fact that his works are "the talk of the town" suggests a contemporary audience during his lifetime or shortly after his peak popularity, firmly anchoring the setting in the mid-to-late 1800s.
